dedupe_keys.name: hillsborough county florida after action report on the community food system and mass feeding after hurricanes helene and milton 2024

description: This case study examines how Hurricanes Helene and Milton, which struck Florida in autumn 2024, affected the community food system and the humanitarian food supply chain in Hillsborough County, around Tampa. The project, led by Elizabeth Dunn of the University of South Florida, interviewed stakeholders from emergency management, government, non-profit organisations, agriculture, food distribution, healthcare, faith-based organisations and other community partners about food system challenges, adaptive strategies and ways to strengthen resilience before, during and after major hurricanes, looking at food availability, accessibility, acceptability and agency across levels of the social-ecological system. Its findings informed the county's after-action report and improvement plan for the community food system and mass feeding, which gives system-level observations, recommendations and mitigation strategies. The qualitative analysis and report are published on the DesignSafe data depot, free to download online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is one county. Caveats: evidence is qualitative from stakeholder interviews, and interview transcripts are not described as public. Simulation uses: documented failure points and mitigation options for food distribution and mass feeding in hurricane response models. Related records: emergency food distribution after Hurricane Ida (case_study-hurricane-ida-new-orleans-food-distribution) and the Houston Food Bank location study (case_study-houston-food-bank-post-disaster-location-allocation) cover related responses.
